recipes.name: Tomato Pie
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound bacon - cooked, drained, and chopped

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In alternating layers, fill pie crust with tomatoes, bacon, green onions, basil, oregano, garlic powder, and red pepper.
Stir together cheese and mayonnaise in a small bowl.
Spread over the top of pie. Cover loosely with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Remove foil and continue baking for 30 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Tomato Pie
raw_recipe.description: This Southern tomato pie with basil, green onions, bacon, and cheese is the perfect recipe for using juicy, ripe, homegrown tomatoes in summertime.

video.description: In this video, join Chef Nicole McLaughlin in this delightful video as she takes you on a culinary journey to make the perfect Tomato Pie. Bursting with the vibrant flavors of fresh summer tomatoes, this savory pie is a true delight for the taste buds. Whether you're a fan of Southern cuisine or simply craving a taste of the garden's harvest, this Tomato Pie recipe is sure to satisfy your cravings. Get ready for a delicious adventure that will leave you wanting seconds!

review.reviewBody: I really liked this! To keep the bottom of the crust from getting soggy brush egg whites on it and bake it alone first.

We love tomato pie! I find that baking the pie crust by the directions, removing from oven and immediately sprinkling 1/2 cup mozzerella cheese over bottom and allowing it to cool for an hour, seals the bottom of the pie and it will not get soggy. Hope this helps.
Wonderful flavor and super easy. Used 50% more on all the fresh herbs except the peppers. Pressed cheese on the bottom and sides of the crust and pre-baked for 8 min. Thanks for sharing!!!

It's a keeper! I did make a few changes though. I pre-baked pie shell, only used 1/4lb bacon, and for the topping, used 1/2c mayo, 1/4c parmigiano and 2 squirts of garlic paste with 2c of Extra sharp cheddar. The filling will spread better! Delicious!!

I did make a couple of changes - confirmed some of them with other reviews...but OMG if this had 10 stars available my family would want me to rate it an 11! 
Changes: Pre baked the crust for 10 min after brushing with egg white / melted cheese on the bottom (used Gruyere) / Started with layer of mixed Radish Greens & Fresh Basil - seasonings / then tomatoes, bacon, scallions...repeated / sprinkled with minced garlic doubled the topping - used 1/2 greek yogurt 1/2 mayo (to add protein). Will be making again as long as our garden is producing tomatoes ( I used a combo of Beefsteak & San Marzano for this dish).

We loved it! I baked my crust first and layered it with mozzarella as another suggested. It helped keep it from turning soggy. I also added a can of chopped green chilies. I only baked it for a total of 30 minutes since I pre-baked the crust. Covered with foil for about 20 minutes. Delish.

Good pie, except for the mayonnaise! I hate mayo so I substituted softened cream cheese and/or Boursin. Very tasty and not watery. I also added cheese on the bottom prior to layering to reduce moisture.

I followed some of the hints of others and the video. I prebaked a Pillsbury pie crust per directions on the box, then let it cool. I salted the tomato slices and laid them out on paper towels for at least 30 minutes, then blotted off the excess juices. No need to peel the tomatoes. I sprinkled a little cheese on the bottom of the crust before layering the tomatoes, bacon, onions and spices. I baked the pie covered with foil for 30 min and uncovered for 20 min. I let it sit for at least 10 minutes before slicing and serving. The cheese and mayo topping was perfect. The fresh basil and the spice blend really gave the pie great flavor. A great way to use my homegrown tomatoes.

We loved the pie it was awesome, superb. The only thing I did different was i bake the crust about 12/15 minutes then took it out of oven and sprinkled some mozzarella cheese in the bottom of pan. It keeps the crust from being soggy. Then you start layering all your goodies as directed. It IA amazing. I will make again very soon. 💖💖

Turned out great, however I did cook the pie crust before hand and toweled my tomatoes off. I used a mixture of cheeses and fresh basil on top. I cooked it covered with foil for 30 and then foil off for about 20 min. Awesome dish.
Outstanding, actually used chopped Italian seasoning I think it spiced it up a little more. Did both pre baked and cover crust with egg white and cheese .
nice for gardens production
This was Delicious. I used "fresh from my garden" tomatoes, basil, oregano, & garlic. Nope, I didn't grow the cheese! Will make again & again.
Made it just the way the recipe said and I thought it was good
Made tomato pie. It was easy to make. Turned out perfect. Read reviews and used some of the suggestions. Was enjoyed and will make again.
This was the best one I've ever made. I didn't have a yellow cheese so I used mozzarella and it was great! In fact that's what I'll use again. yummy!

The written recipe differs from the video, so watch the video for technique, refer to article for measurements. The topping seemed very "pimento cheese-y" to me, so I went ahead and added chopped pimento to it. Needed some color.
This is a recipe to share with your best 🧡 friend no matter the distance.

Made as written with storebought crust, lightly pricked, prebaked pie crust brushed with lightly whipped egg white. Let cool. Layered green onions, bacon, a little of cheese, mayo, & herb mixture, then tomatoes, another light layer of cheese, another layer of tomato, topped with cheese. Only addition I made was a crushed sleeve of Ritz crackers to top in final 10 minutes of baking to give it a little texture. I laid my tomatoes on several layers of paper towels abput an hour before using to drain...and pressed out aome moisture with additional paper towels on top. My pie had minimal if any "seepage". Super delicious - needs to sit 10-15 mins before slicing. So good!!!

Great recipe !!! A senior man I met many years ago told me his mother used to make this for him when he was a kid, and I had always wanted to try it since. The only thing is I probably didn't use more than two large tomatos, as there wasn't enough room for more, and it wasn't clear from the video if you had made two or three complete layers.
